solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One saddled with nasty work heartlessly gags elderly person

indicators.note: heartlessly tells us to drop the central letter of the word for gags

parts.note: OAP is old-age pensioner, a British term for an elderly person

explanation.surface: Someone stuck with an unpleasant job ruthlessly silences an old person.
explanation.walkthrough: JOKES loses its middle letter K to give JOES. JOE SOAP is British slang for the ordinary person who gets landed with the dull or nasty tasks.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Soap is an informal British name for a mug who gets lumbered with the unwanted chores.

clue.text: Change of leadership required by ardent Green

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for ardent must be swapped for a different one

explanation.surface: A keen environmentalist demands a new party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the Z at the head of ZEALOUS for a J. 'Green' looks political but means envious here.
explanation.definitionFit: Green with envy describes someone envious, so green is a familiar synonym for envious.

clue.text: Thrower — man mostly recollected as gardener's friend

indicators.note: recollected suggests these letters are gathered up again in a new order
mostly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A thrower, more or less a man, remembered as a friend to gardeners.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN without its last letter is MA; THROWER plus MA rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Worms aerate and enrich the soil, so gardeners regard them as helpful allies.

clue.text: One eats fish to excess — hospital drama follows

indicators.note: follows places the drama after the excess part

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means done to excess
ER is the American TV hospital drama

explanation.surface: Someone overindulges in fish, and then a hospital crisis ensues.
explanation.definitionFit: This river mammal lives largely on a diet of fish caught in the water.

clue.text: Mischievous pet is fast becoming annoying

indicators.note: mischievous suggests the letters of those two words are playing up and rearranged

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A naughty pet that is going without food grows irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: PET IS rearranged gives PESTI, followed by LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilent in its informal sense means troublesome or irritating, a step up from merely pesky.

clue.text: Splash drops liberally, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily asks for just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: a patter is the sound of many drops falling in quick succession

explanation.surface: A question about what a splash does to drops, scattering them generously.
explanation.walkthrough: The S that begins 'Splash' plus PATTER, many drops falling, give the answer, and the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spatter is to splash or scatter liquid in many small drops over a surface.

clue.text: Plug leakage almost completely — peace at last

indicators.note: almost completely means all of the word except its final letter
at last picks the final letter of peace

explanation.surface: A stopper nearly ends a leak, bringing calm eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: SPILL loses its last L to give SPIL, then add E, the end of 'peace'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spile is a wooden peg or bung used to stop a hole in a cask.

clue.text: Dislike in a way books by one unknown

indicators.note: in puts the books and the one inside the phrase for a way

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a collection of books
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Showing distaste for reading by someone nobody knows.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipathy is a strong aversion, a deep-seated distaste for something or someone.

clue.text: For example book of a film that is in the can

definitions.text: For example book of a film

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for a can

explanation.surface: A film's novelisation, which is safely in the can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the can' sounds like film-making jargon for a finished film; here the can is just a TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is merchandise linked to a film, such as a book of the movie.

clue.text: Got up at nine finally? That's very optimistic

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of nine

explanation.surface: Getting up by nine at last counts as a hopeful outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing things through rose-tinted glasses, roseate means overly hopeful.

clue.text: Father is possessed by island demon

indicators.note: is possessed by puts father inside the island, held by it

parts.note: an ait is a small river island
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: A priest is taken over by a demon from an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An afrit is a powerful evil spirit in Arabic mythology, a kind of jinn.

clue.text: Keyboard that can't do %&*@ could be so inefficient!

definitions.meaning: these symbols need the shift key, so a keyboard without one cannot type them
lacking drive or competence, lazy and ineffective

explanation.walkthrough: The symbols look like a censored swear word, but they are the characters typed with the shift key held down.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiftless describes someone lazy and lacking ambition, so getting little done.

clue.text: Order wee shirt right away or else!

indicators.note: right away means remove R, the abbreviation for right
order tells us to put the letters of the little shirt in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Demanding a small shirt immediately, or there will be trouble!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' looks like 'immediately' but takes R from OR, leaving O; WEE SHIRT rearranged gives THERWISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise and else both mean in a different way or in other circumstances.

clue.text: One eating bamboo soup and assorted preserves

indicators.note: preserves means the clue words keep the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone eating bamboo shoots, soup and a selection of jams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserves' looks like jams but means keeps inside: souP AND Assorted.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda of China feeds almost entirely on bamboo.

clue.text: More than one boat or ship carrying some livestock

indicators.note: carrying puts the animal inside the ship's abbreviation

parts.note: a cow is one of the livestock

explanation.surface: Several vessels, or a ship transporting farm animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Scows are flat-bottomed boats, so the plural means several such vessels.

clue.text: Hat that may be the top of the range?

definitions.text: that may be the top of the range?
definitions.meaning: a chimney pipe rising from a cooking stove, its range

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of the range' suggests the best model, but a range here is a kitchen stove whose flue pipe sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A stovepipe is both a tall silk hat and the flue rising from a stove.

clue.text: Elaborate riff's intro left out of An American in Paris indefinitely?

indicators.note: left out of means a letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: an American living in Paris is an expatriate; 'indefinitely' turns the title into a description, an expatriate

indicators.note: intro means the first letter of riff

explanation.surface: Gershwin's An American in Paris, minus the opening riff, goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: The title evokes the Gershwin piece, but 'an American in Paris' is just an expatriate; remove R to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at length, enlarging on a subject.

clue.text: Exercise run's tough, but don't give up!

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A gruelling training run, but keep at it!
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty rather than quitting.

clue.text: Artist initially wants stupid price for sketch

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word Artist

explanation.surface: A painter is after a silly price for a drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to outline or represent in a faint, sketchy way.

clue.text: Dummy company's strength — hiding millions at first from Revenue

indicators.note: hiding means the company and strength enclose the millions

parts.note: a forte is a strong point

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of Revenue

explanation.surface: A front company hides millions from the tax authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dummy company' suggests a shell firm, but Dummy alone is the definition: a baby's comforter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a dummy is a baby's pacifier, also called a soother.

clue.text: Before it nothing's gained by playing Bach live together

indicators.note: Before puts the anagram ahead of the word it
playing suggests the composer's letters are performed in a different order

explanation.surface: Performing Bach before it yields nothing, as housemates find.
explanation.walkthrough: O added to BACH and rearranged gives COHAB, then IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohabit is to share a home, especially as an unmarried couple.

clue.text: Teenager's hard after year abroad

indicators.note: after places the hard letter following the rest

parts.note: abroad means out, away from home
H is hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A teenager finds things tough after a gap year overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, especially one in their teens.

clue.text: Spooner's far more advanced — you'll get confused

indicators.note: Spooner's means swap the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: way means far, as in way off

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner's ideas are far more advanced, so you'll lose track.
explanation.walkthrough: WAY HIGHER with starting sounds swapped gives HAY WIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To go haywire is to become erratic or muddled, out of control.

clue.text: Principal sign of home's boundary?

indicators.note: principal sign means the first letter of the word home

explanation.surface: Asks what chiefly marks where a house's grounds end.
explanation.walkthrough: H, the start of 'home', plus EDGE; and a hedge is indeed the main sign of a garden's boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of bushes often marks the edge of a garden or property.

clue.text: Letter delivered with sinking heart

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word drops lower in this down clue

explanation.surface: A letter arrives and the reader's spirits fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of DEALT is A; moving it down gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Bet pa switched a crucial boxing fight off

indicators.note: boxing means the word for crucial surrounds the rest
switched means the letters are swapped around

explanation.surface: Father changes his wager on a crucial boxing bout.
explanation.walkthrough: BET PA A rearranged gives EPATBA, placed inside KEY.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep at bay is to hold off an attacker or threat.

clue.text: Stunner oddly rejected monkey nuts

parts.note: KO, a knockout, is a stunning blow

indicators.note: oddly rejected means the odd letters are thrown out, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: An oddly turned-down beauty and a monkey's nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: MONKEY without its 1st, 3rd and 5th letters leaves OKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts and kooky both mean eccentric or slightly crazy in informal speech.

clue.text: Clay walls for Bali's defence

parts.note: Cassius Clay was the boxer Muhammad Ali

indicators.note: walls are the outside letters of the word Bali

explanation.surface: Mud walls protect Bali.
explanation.walkthrough: Clay is not mud but the boxer Cassius Clay, later ALI; the walls of BALI are B and I.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence that one was elsewhere when the crime occurred.

clue.text: Live with collie's barking, becoming aggressive

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: barking, British slang for mad, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Living with a noisy collie makes one combative.
explanation.walkthrough: BE then COLLIES rearranged to LLICOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose means eager to fight, warlike in manner.

clue.text: Asian islands occupied by soldiers on cue, we hear

indicators.note: occupied by puts the soldiers and the cue letter between the islands

parts.note: I is island, twice for islands

indicators.note: we hear means the letter sounds like the word cue

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like Q

explanation.surface: Asian islands overrun by troops right on time, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Q sounds like 'cue'; RA and Q go between I and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is in western Asia, so a person from there is an Asian.

clue.text: For example Lear jet's tail's shabby- looking — not good

indicators.note: tail takes the final letter of jet
not means a letter is removed

explanation.surface: A Learjet's rear is looking tatty and poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear jet' suggests the aircraft, but King Lear is the tragedy; T plus RAGGEDY less one G.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is one of Shakespeare's great tragedies.

clue.text: Effeminate English copper with awkward niece

parts.note: P is a penny, a copper coin

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters of niece are clumsily rearranged

explanation.surface: An English policeman with his ungainly niece.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, PC, but here it is a penny, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicene means having characteristics of both sexes, or lacking masculinity.
